payload.report: The patient has a four-year LVAD and presents with low-grade fever, rapidly progressive renal dysfunction with proteinuria and microhaematuria, positive C. jeikeium blood cultures, low C3, and FDG-PET/CT showing active infection at the driveline, pocket, and outflow cannula. Renal biopsy demonstrates immune-complex crescentic glomerulonephritis with mesangial and subendothelial deposits. These findings strongly support active C. jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related glomerulonephritis. The refined frontier node-13 (score 0.95) is the most credible diagnosis. Primary glomerulonephritis and mechanical renal injury are effectively excluded by the immune-complex pattern, low C3, and active infection. Elevated PR3-ANCA is interpreted as a secondary phenomenon of chronic infection, not primary ANCA-associated disease. Thus the final diagnosis is C. jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related glomerulonephritis.
